channel.title: FAUX NEWS
channel.description: Satire. FauxGrok rewrites right-wing wires. The original headline is always attached.

item.title: "Not to my knowledge" clocks in for another full shift on the homepage
item.description: CLIP SHIFT. The Gateway Pundit has the question, the shrug, and a VIDEO tag. The rumor stays in the chyron. The answer, such as it is, gets a parking spot. They wrote: (VIDEO) Trump Responds to Ilhan Omar Saying “Not to My Knowledge” When Asked if She Married Her Brother

item.title: Someone said "liar" on a stage, so the homepage added explosives
item.description: BOOM. The Gateway Pundit files a debate insult as ordnance, plus a play button. BOOM is doing the reporting. They wrote: BOOM! Mike Rogers Calls Abdul El-Sayed a LIAR to His Face During Debate ‘This is a Pattern’ (VIDEO)

item.title: Kansas candidates spend a debate pretending they have never met their parties
item.description: WHO, US?. Fox News calls it fiery. It is two people backing away from a group photo while control of the Senate gets a mention. They wrote: Kansas Senate rivals distance themselves from party leaders in fiery debate

item.title: Michigan debate shrinks to a panel: America, or a vague menace overseas
item.description: TWO BUTTONS. Breitbart heard a loyalty quiz and took dictation. "Running for Senate" did not fit on the button. They wrote: Mike Rogers Presses El-Sayed in Final Michigan Senate Debate: ‘Are You for America' or 'Terrorist Groups Overseas?’

item.title: A heckler gets reviewed for looks, then a punch gets a highlight reel
item.description: CAPTION BOX. The Gateway Pundit covers a rally scuffle like a boxing undercard, complete with a note on the face. The joke is the caption. They wrote: “Really Unattractive” Leftist Gets Clocked After Screaming at Trump at Rally – Trump Calls Supporter “Evander ‘The Real Deal’ Holyfield” – CROWD ROARS! (VIDEO)

item.title: The raid is a moving box. The homepage is still on the old question.
item.description: CHANGE OF ADDRESS. The Washington Examiner reports an emptied apartment and death threats. The rest of the building has not changed the subject. They wrote: Ilhan Omar vacating DC apartment after federal raid, citing death threats

item.title: Candidate calls a voting bill suppression. The desk faints on time.
item.description: SAY THE LINE. Breitbart prints the flinch as the story. The machinery of the bill can wait until the outrage is plated. They wrote: Michigan Debate: El-Sayed Claims SAVE America Act ‘About Voter Suppression’

item.title: A firing vow, a fraud ghost, and a Democrat who is not in the room
item.description: LEGACY GHOST. Fox News needs a clash, so Minnesota supplies one. The vow is doing most of the work. They wrote: Mass firings vow sparks clash with Klobuchar over Walz fraud legacy

item.title: Fox scoreboard: Trump wins a Michigan debate he did not attend
item.description: OFFSCREEN. The package says he dominates the attacks. The two candidates who were on the stage get a split mention. They wrote: Trump dominates El-Sayed's attacks against Rogers, but GOP rival offers unexpected policy split

item.title: Michigan is declared a needle. Experts are asked if it still moves.
item.description: NEEDLE. The Washington Examiner runs the October classic: the race is finished, and also about to break open. They wrote: Is it too late to move the midterm needle in Michigan?

item.title: France is in the streets. The stake, on this desk, is the NFL pregame.
item.description: PREGAME. PJ Media looks at unrest and finds a Sunday broadcast. The camera truck's travel plans become the American angle. They wrote: Riots Across France Scare Off American Media Covering Sunday’s NFL Game in Paris

item.title: The rally brings the line. The headline brings the can of gasoline.
item.description: MATCHES. The Washington Examiner gives "burn it all down" a full shift in South Carolina. The Senate candidate being boosted shows up, eventually. They wrote: Trump warns Democrats ‘want to burn it all down’ in South Carolina pitch

item.title: Forty defendants, 42 million dollars, and a round number's worth of certainty
item.description: ENFORCEMENT. One America News stacks accusations and a dollar figure in the same breath. Court is a later episode. They wrote: Trump admin. announces enforcement actions against over 40 defendants accused of nearly $42M in SNAP fraud

item.title: The Post scratches its head so a shrug can still lead the page
item.description: HEAD TILT. "Head-scratching" is what you write when the quote dodges and the homepage still needs a temperature. The New York Post supplies the hand to the temple. They wrote: Ilhan Omar gives head-scratching response when asked if she’s related to ex-husband in first interview since DC raid

item.title: A cybercrime crackdown is announced at a table, where computers go to be discussed
item.description: ROUNDTABLE. Breitbart has the president, a roundtable, and a crackdown. The people being cracked down on, being online, did not attend. They wrote: Trump at Roundtable Details Administration's Crackdown on Cybercrime

item.title: A final debate, graded as a loyalty check
item.description: SHOWDOWN. The Washington Times hears a Senate race and files a patriotism quiz. Policy made a brief appearance and was asked to wait outside. They wrote: Rogers questions El-Sayed's loyalty to the U.S. in their final debate showdown

item.title: A show announces the dirt is piling, and declines to say which dirt
item.description: THE PILE. The Blaze has a stack and a type treatment. Viewers are invited to imagine the rest. They wrote: The Abdul El-Sayed dirt keeps PILING UP

item.title: A comedy scolding gets an age joke in the headline, which saves you the clip
item.description: SENIOR MOMENT. The Blaze covers one comic chiding another and labels the whole thing a senior moment. The bit is now optional. They wrote: SENIOR MOMENT: Veteran 'SNL' player breaks ranks to scold Shane Gillis for jokes

item.title: The recap is a stopwatch and the word "lies"
item.description: STOPWATCH. The Daily Wire names a winner before a fact-check graphic could finish loading. Rapid-fire is a format. It is not a finding. They wrote: Mike Rogers Breaks Down El-Sayed With Rapid-Fire List Of Lies At Debate

item.title: A senator's remarks get a CIA costume and the verb "destroy"
item.description: TRENCH COAT. The Federalist hands out a spook title and a threat level. A quote can stretch. It cannot stretch into a covert operation without a wardrobe budget. They wrote: CIA Spook Slotkin Doubles Down On Threat To Destroy Young Conservative Staffers

item.title: One alleged voter, four elections, a headline that already reached a verdict
item.description: FOUR TIMES. The Federalist prints an attorney general's claim as weather. Any hearing is a later episode. They wrote: Indiana AG: Illegal Alien Voted In 4 Federal Elections

item.title: A lawsuit over election power picks up the verb "seizing" for free
item.description: SEIZE. Newsmax has Democrats, a filing, and a president the headline has already caught in the act. They wrote: Dems Sue to Stop Trump From Seizing States' Election Powers

item.title: National Review opens a reminder service for a grudge already on file
item.description: REMINDER. Vivek Ramaswamy has once again reminded the magazine why it keeps a standing column about him. The headline is the piece. They wrote: Vivek Ramaswamy Reminds Voters Why They Never Liked Him

item.title: New Jersey's voter list gets a subpoena and a number with a K in it
item.description: THE ROLL. Just the News, the wire Real America's Voice sends people to read, has the committees, the state, and tens of thousands of something. Whether the matches hold is scheduled for later. They wrote: U.S. House committees subpoena New Jersey in probe of foreigners on voter rolls

item.title: Socialists fail to laugh. Townhall treats that as a finding.
item.description: NOT AMUSED. Larry David wrote something. A faction did not chuckle. Townhall files the silence as a diagnostic test. They wrote: Democratic Socialists Are Not Amused by Larry David's Latest Op-Ed. It's Not Hard to See Why

item.title: A cabinet official is located on a very large boat. The network hits caps lock.
item.description: ALL CAPS. Real America's Voice found Pete Hegseth aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln and printed EXCLUSIVE the way other desks print a leak. The ship was not in hiding. They wrote: EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH SPEAKS OUT FROM ABOARD THE USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN
